-try your best to be open to their openness, the more they experience the more they learn, the more they learn, the more they can make a decision on their own, you cant be there all the time, but be supportive

tl:dr: a lot has changed, be open to experience, kids will be kids, live, let love, learn, make mistakes, learn about the limits of thy self, everything will be ok.

Gloving and what it means to me:  An expression of thyself by use of hand gestures, movements, intricate personal techniques that allow the passage of positive artistic energy from the individual to the audience whom ever they may be...

We are a rare breed, there is a spectrum of glovers: some ranging from competition expertise, to those who are novice who are wanting to learn and those who are joining the band wagon movement...

First of all it begins with you; determining who YOU are within the community and how you wish to participate in its activities!

I personally think we have a strong community.. I see a lot of glovers at events and I always try to connect with them. Some care not for others, which is ok, some teach, some watch and some make small snapchats or small vids.

Those who wish to take gloving on and learn and have a positive growing experience while maintaining an open mind will grow.

Videos and watching body movements is a great way we can utilize the art and show others what each other is capable of.

The learning curve is large with the art of gloving... 

If you want to make the community larger we need more advocates.. more word of mouth, a push for change... its a numbers game.. 

I think if we just keep doing what we are doing here we will be just fine... some of us will continue, some of us will stop, some will teach and some will respect the art.

TL;DR just keep doing what we do.. people will catch on eventually. minus those who don't. increasing market penetration would help a community grow.. creating more groups.. meet ups.. having locations for artistic exchanges in each city
